evidence: src/domain/course.ts: `@Entity()` decorator on `export class Course` declares the domain class as a TypeORM persistence entity (infrastructure responsibility).
src/domain/course.ts: `@Column()` decorator on the `id` property defines how the column is mapped in the database (infrastructure responsibility).
src/domain/course.ts: `admit()` and `release()` hold enrolment business rules, which belong in the domain layer.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: The domain logic in src/domain/course.ts belongs in the domain layer: the admit() method enforces the published and capacity rules, and release() decrements enrolment. The problem is that the class also maps itself to the database. The TypeORM decorators @Entity() on class Course and @Column() on the id field make this domain entity the persistence model, and that is an infrastructure job. This mapping should live in an infrastructure ORM entity or schema that maps to and from the domain Course. Whether domain code may import 'typeorm' at all is a dependency-direction question and is out of scope here. The failure is that the file itself carries ORM mapping.
